moves_applied.reason: Liebig/Kjeldahl/Carius estimations with numericals are calculation-based quantitative analysis rather than hands-on bench technique, making B3 (quantitative methods) the best legal home.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_wanted: Chemical kinetics; acids, bases & pH; electrochemistry
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Compound topic practicals on rates, pH and voltaic cells; file with those chemistry topics, not measurement/data.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: This is a compound practical generating measurements, graphs and observations, and the map deliberately houses experiments in B4 rather than dispersing them to C8, C7/H-ACIDBASE or C5/H-ECHEM.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Defining mineral/ore and naming ores is foundational metallurgy theory, not an application context.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Defining mineral/ore and naming common ores is contextual raw-material knowledge for extraction chemistry, and with no metallurgy node B6 (applications & contexts) is the best available fit.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Chloroform/iodoform preparation is core organic reaction chemistry; only freon/DDT effects are contextual.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The unit is dominated by uses, structures and environmental effects of polyhalogen compounds, so B6 remains best despite the brief chloroform/iodoform preparation clause.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Vitamin classification and deficiency diseases belong with biomolecules, not applications.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Vitamin solubility classes and deficiency diseases are health-and-nutrition context, best housed in B6 absent any biomolecules node.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Normality, equivalents and acid/alkali/redox equivalent weights are titration chemistry; only molarity/molality/mole fraction fit the mole hub.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Normality, molarity, molality, mole fraction and equivalent weights are all amount-of-substance counting conventions bridging particles to mass and volume, which is exactly the mole hub's remit.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Coloured compounds, catalysis, alloys, magnetism are transition-metal descriptive chemistry, filed under d-block, not periodicity.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The statement explicitly teaches property trends across the 3d/4d/5d series arising from recurring d-electron configurations, which is precisely periodicity as this map defines it.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_wanted: Transition elements (d- and f-block / inner transition metals)
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Lanthanoid/actinoid configurations and reactivity belong with f-block elements, not general periodic trends.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: f-block configurations, oxidation-state patterns and lanthanoid contraction are configuration-driven periodic trends, best filed under periodicity with no f-block node available.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Tetravalency, catenation and carbon chain/ring bonding patterns launch organic chemistry, not general bonding theory.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Tetravalency, catenation and the formation of single, double and triple bonds are core covalent-bonding concepts squarely within C2's scope.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Structural formulae of alkanes/alkenes/alkynes and chain/position isomerism are hydrocarbon topics, not bonding principles.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Drawing hydrocarbon structural formulae and recognising chain/position isomerism is molecular-structure content, best kept at C2 rather than treated as mere symbolic convention.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Vital force history and reasons for organic abundance belong to organic chemistry's origin, not bonding.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The reasons given for organic abundance (tetravalency, catenation, isomerism, multiple bonding) are bonding and structure principles, so C2 is the best legal home even with the historical framing.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Ligand denticity, coordination number, oxidation state and IUPAC naming of complexes are coordination chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Ligand denticity, chelation, coordination number and complex composition are principally bonding and molecular-structure concepts, despite the nomenclature component.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Werner, VBT and crystal field splitting explaining colour/magnetism of complexes belong under coordination chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Werner theory, valence bond theory and crystal field theory are models of bonding and electronic structure used to interpret coordination complexes.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_wanted: Organic chemistry fundamentals – classification of organic compounds
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Structural taxonomy of organic compounds; teaches classification, not how structure determines properties.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The classification is organized around carbon frameworks and functional groups that underpin structure-dependent family behavior, making C3 the closest legal home.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Carbohydrate classification and structure elucidation via reactions; no property relationship taught.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Aldose and ketose identity, ring forms and glycosidic linkages are molecular-architecture distinctions that determine carbohydrate classification and behavior.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Protein/amino-acid topic content; only denaturation touches structure–property; rest is biomolecules.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Amino-acid ionization, protein structural hierarchy and denaturation directly connect molecular structure to physical and biological properties.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Descriptive DNA/RNA structure; belongs in nucleic-acid topic, not structure–property concept.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Base composition and DNA and RNA architecture are the structural basis for nucleic-acid identity and function, fitting the structure–property node.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Strong/weak/non-electrolyte classification is behaviour in electrolysis context, not a states-and-solutions origin concept.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Electrolyte strength follows from the particles present in solution and their dissociation and conduction rather than from potential-driven redox.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Compound preparation, properties and uses; no mechanism or change-classification concept.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Although framed around ammonia, the unit is dominated by its preparations and characteristic chemical reactions, so broad chemical change is the best legal home.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Industrial manufacture and acid behaviour; compound study, not mechanism theory.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The manufacture and acid, oxidising and dehydrating behavior of sulfuric acid primarily concern chemical transformations rather than a more specific legal concept node.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Preparation and reactions of specific hydrocarbons; compound-class study.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The unit centers on hydrocarbon preparation and combustion, substitution and addition reactions, making C5 the best available home.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Ethanol preparation, properties, uses; functional-group compound study.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Ethanol preparation and its combustion, sodium reaction, esterification and dehydration are principally chemical-change content, so C5 remains appropriate.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Nomenclature, isomerism, conformations dominate; not mechanism concepts.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Despite its nomenclature and conformation preamble, the unit's substance is preparations (decarboxylation, Kolbe, Wurtz, Corey-House) and reactions (radical halogenation, combustion, pyrolysis, oxidation) — bond-breaking and bond-making chemistry that belongs to C5 in a map with no hydrocarbon node.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Alkene preparation, reactions, tests; functional-group unit despite one mechanism mention.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The unit is dominated by addition reactions, ozonolysis, oxidation and polymerisation framed around the electrophilic addition mechanism, which is precisely C5's pathway view of chemical change.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Alkyne chemistry as a compound class; belongs with hydrocarbons.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Preparation, acetylide formation, addition and oxidation of alkynes are reaction chemistry — bonds breaking and forming — so C5 is the best legal home absent an alkyne chapter node.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Benzene aromaticity and substitution chemistry; aromatic unit content.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The core of the unit is electrophilic aromatic substitution taught explicitly with its mechanism, making C5 the best fit even though aromaticity itself touches bonding.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Classification, C-X bond, preparations; functional-group unit, not mechanisms.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The unit's load is preparation of haloalkanes via multiple synthetic routes, i.e. chemical change along reaction pathways, which C5 covers and no chapter-style node exists to rival it.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Haloarene preparations and reactions; named-reaction compound chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Sandmeyer/Gattermann preparations plus electrophilic and nucleophilic substitution chemistry are mechanism-governed bond changes, squarely within C5.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Alcohol classification and preparation methods; functional-group study.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: A catalogue of preparative reactions (hydration, Grignard, hydrolysis, reduction) is reaction-pathway content, best housed at C5 since the roster has no alcohols node.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Alcohol properties and Lucas distinction; compound chemistry despite mechanism words.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Esterification and dehydration are taught with their mechanisms alongside oxidation and substitution reactions, so the unit is mechanism-driven chemistry belonging to C5.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Phenol preparation, acidity, named reactions; phenol unit content.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Phenol's preparations, electrophilic substitution, Kolbe and Reimer-Tiemann reactions dominate the unit; its acidity note alone does not outweigh C5 as the reaction-chemistry home.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Williamson synthesis and ether reactions; functional-group unit.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Williamson synthesis and ether cleavage/oxidation reactions are bond-forming and bond-breaking processes, making C5 the best available node.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Preparative routes to carbonyls; compound-class study.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Preparative routes to aldehydes and ketones from varied substrates are synthetic reaction chemistry, which the mechanism-organised map places at C5 by design.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Named carbonyl reactions and distinguishing tests; carbonyl unit, not general mechanism theory.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Every item named — nucleophilic addition, aldol, Cannizzaro, iodoform, oxidation and Clemmensen/Wolff-Kishner reduction — is bond-breaking/forming pathway chemistry, and the map has no carbonyl chapter node, so C5 is the correct mechanism home.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Specific compound's chemistry; aromatic aldehyde unit.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Benzaldehyde's oxidation, reduction, nucleophilic addition, Cannizzaro, benzoin, Perkin and electrophilic substitution are all reaction-mechanism content, so absent a legal 'benzaldehyde' node C5 remains best.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Acid preparation, acidity, derivatives; functional-group unit.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The unit is dominated by preparative and derivatisation reactions (decarboxylation, HVZ, ring substitution) rather than proton-transfer speciation, so C5 fits better than C7/H-ACIDBASE and no carboxylic-acid chapter node exists.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Amine classification, preparation, basicity; functional-group study.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The bulk is preparation via named transformations (Hofmann degradation, Gabriel synthesis, reductions) — mechanism chemistry under C5 — with basicity comparison too minor to displace it to C7/H-ACIDBASE.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Hinsberg test and amine reactions; compound-class chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Hinsberg, alkylation, acylation, nitrous acid and carbylamine chemistry are reaction pathways distinguishing amine classes, squarely C5 mechanism content with no legal 'amines' node available.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Aniline preparation and reactions; specific compound study.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Aniline's reduction-based preparation and its diazotisation, acylation, carbylamine and substitution reactions are all mechanism content, making C5 the best legal home absent an aniline chapter node.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Diazonium salt synthesis chemistry; belongs with amines unit.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Diazonium chemistry (Sandmeyer, Gattermann, Balz-Schiemann, coupling) and cyanide/isocyanide preparation are named synthetic reaction pathways, exactly what C5 houses in a mechanism-organised map.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Bauxite purification and Hall-Heroult extraction are metallurgy; only the electrolytic step touches electrochemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The unit's assessable core is Hall-Héroult electrolytic reduction with cell structure and electrode reactions — redox driven by applied potential — so with no metallurgy node, C5/H-ECHEM is the best mechanistic home.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Hydrogen preparation and metal activity series, not redox concepts
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Metal/water, metal/acid and metal/alkali hydrogen evolution via the activity series is electron-transfer displacement chemistry governed by oxidation-state change, which is precisely C5/H-REDOX territory.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Ore dressing, roasting, calcination, reduction — extraction chemistry
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Roasting, calcination and oxide reduction by H2/C/CO or electrolysis are unified by reduction chemistry, so absent a metallurgy node C5/H-REDOX best captures the unit's chemical mechanism.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: HNO3 preparation and properties; oxidising action is only one facet
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The stated study centres on HNO3 as an oxidising agent with Cu, C and S (with preparation and acidity secondary), so C5/H-REDOX is the best legal home since no p-block compound node exists.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: KMnO4 structure and extraction is transition-metal compound study
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Although structure and extraction are included, the unit's unifying chemistry is permanganate's medium-dependent oxidising behaviour and redox-titration use.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: K2Cr2O7 structure, extraction and interconversion is d-block chemistry
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Dichromate's oxidising action and titrimetric applications dominate the unit, with the chromate–dichromate equilibrium serving that redox context.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Stability constants and their analytical/biological uses are taught within coordination chemistry, not the equilibrium unit.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Stability constants are equilibrium constants for complex formation, so C7 is the best legal home despite the coordination-compound applications.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Acetic acid structure, esterification with alcohol and uses are organic chemistry, not general acid-base theory.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Acetic acid's defining proton-transfer reactions with indicators and alkalis make acid–base chemistry the best available legal home, notwithstanding esterification and uses.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_wanted: Study of compounds – hydrogen chloride (non-metal compounds)
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Gas preparation, fountain experiment and chloride-ion tests are compound study; only partly acid properties.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The unit spans preparation and ion tests, but hydrogen chloride's acidic behaviour in water and proton-transfer reaction with ammonia anchor it most closely to acid–base chemistry.

blind_placement_audit_v9_cohort.policy: MOVE verdicts applied; UPHOLD objections disclosed verbatim, units not moved. Both rates reported; the blind rate is not the roster-aware rate and neither replaces the other.

pep_crosswalk_audit.method: R1 blind (node title + section titles only), R2 roster-aware challenge with UPHOLD/MOVE/DROP; the map has no chapter-topic nodes, so taxonomy objections are settled against the actual roster

moves_applied.reason: The Fe/Fe2+/Fe3+ interconversions this pair was carrying are canonical redox teaching content, making the redox hub—not periodicity—the precise mechanism home.

drops_applied.reason: Topic 2 is purely oxygen's physical/chemical properties and reaction concepts, fully carried by C5; oxygen's uses are treated in Topic 1, so B6 adds noise here.

The section teaches salts' properties, reactions (double displacement, carbonate test) and everyday uses — C5 carries the chemistry, the 'in life' uses would be B6's remit if anything, and nothing develops C1's atomic/particulate/composition strand.
Descriptive sodium and sodium-compound chemistry is reactions-of-substances content fully covered by C5, and no periodic trends are taught in this section.
Chlorine preparation and properties are reaction chemistry already housed at C5; periodic law appears in a later chapter, so this tag is noise.
Physical/chemical changes and properties are phenomenological chemical-change content already covered by C5, with no structural reasoning to justify a structure-property tag.
The grade-9 nutrient survey is health and daily-life application content fully carried by B6, with no structure-determines-property reasoning present.
Addition and condensation polymerization methods are reaction-mechanism chemistry already housed at C5, and structure-property treatment of polymer materials comes in later sections.
Observing luster, conductivity and ductility involves no oxidation-state change, and the B2 and C3 mappings already cover the practical and structure-property content.

The bare 'Topic 2 Solubility' title in this foundational chapter reads as general dissolving/saturation/solubility-factor content, which C4 already covers; there is no evidence of Ksp or equilibrium-constant treatment that would justify the solubility-equilibria node.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Electrolytes, ionic equations, and reaction conditions are aqueous reaction chemistry, not naming or symbolic convention.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Writing ionization equations and net ionic equations is a core taught skill of this section and is exactly the symbolic-convention content B1 houses, while C5 already carries the reaction chemistry.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Carbon bonding, skeletons, and isomerism are organic structure content; belongs under organic chemistry, not conventions.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The section teaches organic representation conventions — structural and condensed formulas plus habitual alkane naming (正/异/新) — a legitimate B1 component alongside the structure content carried by C2.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Combustion conditions belong under oxygen/combustion chemistry; being a lab activity doesn't make it methodology.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: This is a dedicated student experiment session whose content IS controlled-variable inquiry into combustion conditions (the chemistry itself was taught in the preceding topic), so B4/B2 is the correct profile.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Rate-factor experiment lives in chemical kinetics; activity label alone doesn't justify this node.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: C8 already carries the kinetics concepts, and this lab-activity section's controlled-variable design and rate measurement/data work are precisely B4's remit.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: CO2/CO compound properties dominate; uses and greenhouse context are incidental.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The section contains a named subsection on CO2's effects on life and environment (uses, dry ice, fire extinguishing, greenhouse effect) plus CO poisoning context — substantial applications content, not incidental.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Sulfur, SO2, sulfuric acid transformations are systematic element chemistry despite industrial framing.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: In an explicitly chemical-industry-framed chapter, sulfur and SO2 uses, sulfuric acid production context, and pollution framing give B6 real content beside C5's transformations.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: NH3, HNO3, NOx chemistry is core element chemistry; acid-rain context is peripheral.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Nitrogen fixation (雷雨发庄稼), the synthetic-ammonia industry, fertilizer use, and NOx-driven acid rain are explicit teaching threads, making B6 legitimate alongside C5.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Carbohydrate structure and reactions belong to organic/biomolecular chemistry, not applications.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Blood-glucose/medical and food contexts for monosaccharides/disaccharides and cellulose material applications (nitrocellulose, rayon) are taught here, giving B6 genuine content beside C3's structure-property core.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Air composition, gases, pollution; belongs under mixtures/atmosphere, not atoms or particulate models.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Air's fixed percentage composition and the mixture-versus-pure-substance classification taught in this topic are matter-composition content squarely inside C1's remit, and no better legal node exists.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Classification, transformation, colloids; belongs under matter classification/mixtures, not atomic structure.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Classification of matter into elements/compounds/mixtures is composition-and-particulate-nature content that is core to C1, while the colloid/dispersion portion is already housed at C4.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Element concept and symbols; periodic table only skimmed—belongs under matter composition/basic concepts.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The section's brief periodic-table introduction (atomic number, periods/groups lookup) is genuine seed periodicity content that C1 alone does not capture.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Alkane nomenclature, properties, substitution reactions — organic hydrocarbon chemistry, only minor structure content belongs here.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Alkane sigma-bond skeletons, tetrahedral carbon, and chain isomerism are substantive C2 bonding-and-structure content, even though the reaction portions could also be tagged at C5.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Alkene/alkyne addition, polymerization, isomerism — organic reaction chemistry, not general bonding and structure.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: C=C and C≡C pi bonding plus cis-trans isomerism are squarely bonding/structure content, while the addition and polymerization reactions are already carried by C5.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Basic nutrients again; food chemistry with minimal structure–property reasoning.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Here nutrient chemistry is taught through functional-group structure (glucose's aldehyde group, ester linkages, amino acids) determining characteristic reactions and properties, a legitimate structure-property home beyond B6's context.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Lab merely measures metal properties; structure absent, only the property side.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The laboratory comparison of metallic luster, conductivity, malleability, and related properties legitimately carries the property side of structure-property relationships, while B2 covers only the procedure.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Separation techniques (filtration, adsorption, distillation); mixture purification, not interparticle interactions or solution chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Water purification teaches separation of mixtures and solutions through particle size, adsorption, and phase change, placing its conceptual content within C4 alongside B2.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Substance taxonomy and reaction transformation dominate; only colloid/dispersion segment tangentially touches states.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The section's treatment of dispersions and colloids directly concerns particle-scale mixture behavior and states, so C4 is not redundant with C1.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Descriptive oxygen properties; substance chemistry, not the concept of chemical change or mechanism.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Oxygen's descriptive chemistry is taught through its characteristic reactions and chemical changes, which the fixed map assigns to C5.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Laboratory preparation of a specific gas; substance prep, not reaction-mechanism content.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Oxygen preparation combines laboratory technique with decomposition reactions and observable chemical change, making C5 a legitimate conceptual home.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Water's composition via electrolysis; substance-centric, belongs with water/hydrogen chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Electrolysis is used here as decomposition evidence for water's composition rather than as a study of electrochemical principles, so C5 appropriately carries the reaction content.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: CO2 preparation investigation; gas-prep practical chemistry, not mechanisms.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Carbon dioxide production is organized around the acid-carbonate reaction and chemical change, while B2 carries the apparatus and investigation technique.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Properties of CO2 and CO; descriptive compound chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The properties of carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide are conveyed through their characteristic reactions and conversions, which belong in C5 under the fixed map.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Common salts and their uses; descriptive salt chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The common-salts section teaches representative salt reactions and transformations, so C5 remains legitimate despite the everyday applications context.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Sodium element chemistry; belongs under alkali metals, not change/mechanism.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Sodium and its compounds are taught through characteristic reactions and conversions, while C1/H-PERIOD supplies the alkali-metal context rather than replacing C5.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Chlorine element chemistry; halogen descriptive chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Chlorine and its compounds are taught through their characteristic reaction chemistry, with C1/H-PERIOD capturing halogen context and C5 carrying the transformations.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Iron and compounds; transition-metal descriptive chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: With no chapter-topic node allowed, the descriptive reaction chemistry of iron and its compounds (oxidation, Fe2+/Fe3+ conversions) correctly lives at C5, while C1/H-PERIOD covers its periodic placement.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Sulfur compounds; descriptive nonmetal chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Sulfur and its compounds are taught through their reactions (combustion, SO2/sulfuric acid chemistry), which per the settled structure reside at C5, with B6 carrying industrial/environmental context.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Nitrogen compounds; descriptive nonmetal chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Nitrogen descriptive chemistry (NH3, NOx, HNO3 reactions) is reaction chemistry of substances and belongs at C5, with B6 covering applications like fertilizers.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Ethylene and polymer materials; organic substance chemistry, not mechanism per se.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Ethylene's addition reactions and addition polymerization are precisely the reaction-mechanism content C5 houses, while B6 covers the polymer-materials applications.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Ethanol/acetic acid properties; organic compound chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Ethanol oxidation and esterification of acetic acid are reaction chemistry properly homed at C5, complementing C7/H-ACIDBASE which carries acetic acid's ionization.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Properties experiment for ethanol/acetic acid; substance-properties lab.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: This properties experiment teaches the reaction chemistry of ethanol and acetic acid (Na reaction, combustion, esterification, acidity), so C5 is a legitimate home and the section's only crosswalk node.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Alkene/alkyne family chemistry; belongs in organic hydrocarbons node.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: No organic-hydrocarbon node exists, and alkene/alkyne chemistry is taught via addition, oxidation, and polymerization reactions, which live at C5 while C2 carries their bonding/structure.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Aromatic hydrocarbon chemistry; organic family node.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Aromatic hydrocarbon chemistry centers on benzene's substitution and addition reactions, which per the fixed structure belong at the mechanism node C5.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Halogenated hydrocarbons; organic functional-family chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Halogenated hydrocarbons are defined by their nucleophilic substitution and elimination reactions, canonical C5 mechanism content in the absence of any functional-family node.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Alcohols and phenols; organic functional-family chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Alcohol and phenol chemistry (substitution, elimination, oxidation, weak acidity reactions) is reaction-mechanism content that correctly resides at C5.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Aldehydes and ketones; organic functional-family chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Aldehyde and ketone chemistry is taught through carbonyl addition and oxidation/reduction reactions, which the settled map places at C5.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Carboxylic acids and derivatives; organic functional-family chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: With no organic node in the fixed map, carboxylic acid and derivative reaction chemistry (esterification, hydrolysis, acid reactions) is exactly the substance-reaction content C5 is designated to host.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Organic synthesis design; belongs in organic synthesis node, not general change/mechanism.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Organic synthesis design is reaction-mechanism and chemical-change content, and no dedicated organic synthesis node exists, so C5 is the correct legal home.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Ethyl acetate preparation lab; specific esterification experiment.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Preparing ethyl acetate teaches the esterification reaction and its reversibility, so C5 legitimately complements the B2 practical-technique mapping.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Functional-group identification lab; qualitative organic analysis.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Functional-group identification works through characteristic test reactions, which is reaction chemistry properly housed at C5 alongside the B2 technique mapping.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Sugar properties experiment; biomolecule descriptive chemistry.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Sugar properties (reducing-sugar oxidation, hydrolysis) are descriptive compound reaction chemistry that the rules assign to C5, with B2 carrying the lab technique.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Polymer synthesis methods; polymer chemistry node, not general reaction mechanisms.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Addition and condensation polymerization are reaction mechanisms, so C5 is the designated home while C3 already covers polymer structure-property aspects.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Broad energetics survey (heat, enthalpy); galvanic cells only one subtopic. Home is thermochemistry/energy-changes node.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: The section explicitly covers conversion of chemical energy into electrical energy via galvanic (primary) cells, making electrochemistry a legitimate secondary home alongside C6 thermochemistry.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Metal resource utilization and corrosion protection is applied/industrial chemistry, no stoichiometric content.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: This topic includes the iron-smelting worked example requiring mass-yield calculation with impure ore, a genuine stoichiometry component alongside the redox and applications mappings.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Ethanol and acetic acid is organic functional-group chemistry, not acid-base theory.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Acetic acid's acidity (indicator and carbonate reactions, comparison with carbonic acid) is proton-transfer chemistry legitimately hosted at the acid-base hub while C5 carries the organic reaction chemistry.

chapter_taxonomy_dissent.auditor_why: Carboxylic acids and derivatives (esters etc.) is organic chemistry, not acid-base equilibrium.
chapter_taxonomy_dissent.uphold_reason: Carboxylic acid acidity and relative acid strength are explicitly taught content in this section, so the acid-base hub legitimately carries that portion while C5 carries the derivative reaction chemistry.
